blockingIssues.description: VAL-ENGINE-016 is not actually implemented. The artifact bundle is just a verbatim scenario copy plus loose fixture copies, so it never vendors the product chart or rewrites relative paths for replay. All shipped sample scenarios still point `product.chart` at `./chart`, and the advertised replay entrypoint (`apply-scenario.sh`) only walks `.cluster.preinstall`, so a reviewer cannot reproduce the original helm releases from `PROJECT_DIR=<tmp>/artifacts` as required.

The `applied-overrides.yaml` writer does not compute a final merged `helm_values` map. It emits the product values file and `.product.set` as separate YAML fragments under `helm_values:` instead of merging them, so scenarios that use both sources will produce ambiguous/non-flattened overrides and violate the artifact contract's required final merged shape.

nonBlockingIssues.description: The manifest capture step claims to record secret metadata only, but `kubectl get secrets -o yaml` writes full Secret objects into the artifact bundle. That can leak credentials or tokens into `reports/run-*` artifacts.

The new bats file never exercises the runtime replay path from an artifact bundle: its own coverage header omits VAL-ENGINE-016, and the individual cases are mostly source-grep checks. That made it easy for the missing replay implementation to ship unnoticed.

codeReview.summary: The commit adds artifact directories, snapshot metadata, repo-add cleanup, and CSV quoting support, but it misses the two core F1.4 promises: the bundle is not replayable from `artifacts/` alone, and `applied-overrides.yaml` is not a true final merge. The added test coverage is largely structural, so these runtime gaps were not caught before handoff.

issues.description: Replay from artifacts alone is broken. `run-scenario.sh` copies the input scenario verbatim into `artifacts/scenario.yaml`, but does not vendor the product chart or rewrite relative references to the copied fixture files. `apply-scenario.sh` then only replays `.cluster.preinstall`, so the contract in VAL-ENGINE-016 / mission artifact reproducibility cannot succeed for the sample scenarios that still reference `./chart`.

The override artifact is not the requested final merge. Instead of using `yq` or Helm to build one merged mapping, the function appends the values-file YAML and the `.product.set` YAML under the same `helm_values:` key. That does not flatten nested keys and will produce duplicate/ambiguous mappings whenever both inputs are present.

The manifest dump stores full Secret YAML even though the comment says metadata only. Because these bundles are meant for review and sharing, emitting entire Secret objects is an unnecessary exposure risk.

The test suite is largely a static grep audit of script source and never runs the contract's replay scenario. That is why the bundle can claim VAL-ENGINE-016 coverage in the handoff even though no test proves it.
